### F1-Score
The F1-Score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It balances precision and recall when the class distribution is heavily skewed or imbalanced:
$$\text{F1} = 2 \times \frac{\text{Precision} \times \text{Recall}}{\text{Precision} + \text{Recall}}$$ ### ROC-AUC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Cha
### ROC-AUC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve) ROC-AUC measures the model's ability to discrimina

ROC-AUC measures the model's ability to discriminate between positive and negative classes across all possible classification thresholds. A random guess achieves an AUC of 0.50, whereas a perfect classifier achieves an AUC of 1.00. ---

1. **Context Relevance (Retrieval)**:
   Measures whether the retrieved chunks are relevant to the user query. If retrieval returns irrelevant context, the LLM will either fail to answer or suffer from the "lost in the middle" effect. 2. **Groundedness / Faithfulness (Hallucination Co

2. **Groundedness / Faithfulness (Hallucination Control)**:
   Measures whether every claim made in the generated answer can be strictly traced back to the retrieved context chunks. If an answer contains facts not present in the context, it is deemed unfaithful or hallucinated. 3. **Answer Relevance (Generation)**:

3. **Answer Relevance (Generation)**:
   Measures whether the final response directly addresses the user's initial question without drifting into tangential topics.
Week 8 Concept Guide: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Evaluation 1. Definition of RAG
1. Definition of RAG Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI arch

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI architecture that combines an information retrieval system with a generative large language model (LLM). Instead of relying exclusively on facts stored in

Instead of relying exclusively on facts stored in the model weights during pre-training, RAG dynamically fetches relevant text chunks from an external database or corpus at query time, appends them to the prompt context, and instructs the LLM to generate grounded answers citing the retrieved sources.

Precision is the fraction of relevant instances among the retrieved or positive instances. Formally, Precision = True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives). Recall is the fraction of relevant instances that were retrieved, defined as Recall = True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives). High recall means the system misses very few positive cases. 3. Classification versus Regression

5. Vector Databases and FAISS
FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is a library developed by Meta AI for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. - Flat Index (IndexFlatIP): An exact search index.

- Flat Index (IndexFlatIP): An exact search index. It does not use approximations or clustering shortcuts. It compares the query vector against every single vector in the index. When vectors are L2-normalized, the inner product (IP) equals cosine similarity. IndexFlatIP achieves 100% recall and is the optima
IndexFlatIP achieves 100% recall and is the optimal choice for corpora below 100,000 vectors. - IVF Index (IndexIVFFlat): An inverted file index

- IVF Index (IndexIVFFlat): An inverted file index using k-means clustering to partition the vector space into Voronoi cells. At query time, only vectors inside the nearest nprobe clusters are evaluated. It offers immense speedup for millions of vectors at the cost of approximate recall. - Top-k Retrieval: The parameter k determines how
- Top-k Retrieval: The parameter k determines how many closest chunks are retrieved from the index and supplied to the augmented prompt.
